content:
Over the years, Apple has continued to add more customization options to iOS. First, in iOS 16, we regained full lock screen personalization, then iOS 18 brought icon tinting, iOS 26 introduced transparent icons, and iOS 27 brought full-screen Liquid Glass sliders.

iPhones have become more personal over time, and that's a good thing. Now that we can tint the icons on the home screen — why not extend that to the entire operating system?

iOS 27 hasn't been released to the public yet, so I may be getting ahead of myself when thinking about what Apple could do in the next version of its software. Even so, I think adding themed app color schemes beyond light and dark mode would be a sensible next step.

I'm basically asking for a copy of Material You's design on iOS, but based on icon colors rather than the wallpaper — though Apple should offer that option too. Apple debuted an option last year to match icons to the color of the MagSafe case you're using, which would also pair perfectly with this whole system of color themes.

It's also worth noting that Apple introduced color themes earlier this year at WWDC for Xcode, its integrated development environment for building Apple software. There are tons of gorgeous options there — why not bring that fun to the iPhone? At this point, even the Mac already lets you set a system-wide tint for third-party apps.

Summary

Overall, I just think color themes on iOS would look really good and would be another step toward giving users more room to customize.

What are your thoughts on adding color themes to iOS and iPadOS? Let us know in the comments.
